definition.title: Healthy-adult pulmonary 0D reference with bounded flow and age conditioning

baseline_cardiac_output.derivation: Six L/min is the locked v1 nominal resting value within the published 4-8 L/min normal interval and is the denominator of the flow ratio.

left_atrial_pressure.derivation: Eight mmHg is the locked v1 nominal pressure sink below the published PAWP upper limit of 15 mmHg; PAWP remains a left-atrial pressure surrogate.

pulmonary_vascular_resistance.derivation: The locked v1 baseline is 1.2 Wood units within the published 0.3-2.0 Wood-unit normal interval; the flow rule multiplies rather than replaces it.

pulmonary_arterial_compliance.derivation: The locked v1 baseline is 5 mL/mmHg above the published normal lower limit of 2.3 mL/mmHg; the flow rule multiplies rather than replaces it.

pulmonary_transit_time.derivation: The v1 median right-to-left ventricular first-pass pulmonary transit time is retained; no unsupported exercise transit rule is introduced.

right_lung_perfusion_fraction.derivation: The v1 supine RPA/(RPA+LPA) aggregate split is retained; exercise redistribution remains outside this increment.

mean_pulmonary_arterial_pressure_target.derivation: The unchanged baseline prediction is 15.2 mmHg; flow adaptation is exactly neutral at the reference cardiac output.

reference_cardiac_output.derivation: The locked MEHLISSA resting reference of 6 L/min is retained as the denominator even when an independent validation flow is supplied as the simulated condition.

resistance_exponent.derivation: Power-law exponent ln((1.4 WU)/(1.7 WU))/ln((16.2 L/min)/(6.2 L/min)), using healthy-control mean total pulmonary resistance and cardiac output at rest and peak exercise; source SDs are retained in the model card but not propagated into the exponent.

compliance_exponent.derivation: Power-law exponent ln((5.1 mL/mmHg)/(9.7 mL/mmHg))/ln((16.2 L/min)/(6.2 L/min)), using healthy-control mean pulmonary arterial compliance and cardiac output at rest and peak exercise; source SDs are not propagated into the exponent.

maximum_flow_ratio.derivation: The adaptation is capped at the source cohort mean peak-to-rest cardiac-output ratio, 16.2/6.2. Below the MEHLISSA baseline ratio of one, adaptation is disabled to avoid unsupported low-flow extrapolation.

default_age_years.derivation: The midpoint of the 50-59-year reference band supplies a reproducible default; simulations should replace it with the represented cohort or subject age.

minimum_supported_age_years.derivation: Lower boundary of the reported healthy-adult study age range; extrapolation below it is rejected.

older_lower_age_years.derivation: The published 60-69 and over-70 strata are pooled into the independently locked 60-and-older MEHLISSA band.

maximum_supported_age_years.derivation: Upper boundary of the reported healthy-adult study age range; extrapolation above it is rejected.

young_resistance_multiplier.derivation: Published under-40 PASP/CO mean 3.8 divided by the sample-size-weighted 40-59 reference mean (93*4.0 + 127*4.2)/(93+127) = 4.115454545.

older_resistance_multiplier.derivation: The sample-size-weighted 60-and-older PASP/CO mean (127*4.5 + 84*4.8)/(127+84) = 4.619431280 divided by the 40-59 reference mean 4.115454545.

validity.population: healthy adults aged 18-85 represented by guideline ranges and healthy-volunteer cohorts
validity.physiological_state: mean-flow rest through bounded peak-exercise flow ratio with three age bands; measured PAWP may be supplied as an external boundary
validity.description: Two-element mean pulmonary Windkessel with flow-dependent PVR and arterial compliance, a separately calibrated age multiplier on PVR, a fixed or externally conditioned left-atrial pressure sink, total pulmonary transit delay, and fixed right/left flow partition.

limitations: This is a research reference candidate, not a diagnostic or treatment model.
The model resolves mean pressure only and omits pulsatile ventricular and valve dynamics even though compliance was derived from pulsatile measurements.

Claessen et al. reported total pulmonary resistance for healthy controls because wedge pressure was unavailable; its rest-to-exercise ratio is used as a proxy for the PVR multiplier and this methodological mismatch is explicit.
Power-law exponents are point estimates derived from cohort means; covariance and uncertainty were unavailable and are not propagated.
Flow adaptation is clamped to the interval from the MEHLISSA resting reference to the Claessen cohort mean peak-to-rest flow ratio and must not be extrapolated beyond it.
The Claessen cohort was small, predominantly male, and younger than the independent Bentley validation cohort.
Kane et al. used non-invasive Doppler PASP and cardiac-output estimates; PASP/CO is only a total-load proxy for an age effect on mean PVR, not an invasive PVR measurement.

Kane reports 467 participants in the abstract and Table 1 but 469 in the results text; the five published Table 2 age-stratum counts also sum to 469, and those table counts are used only for the declared weighted means.
Age conditioning is stepwise rather than continuous, modifies resistance only, and propagates neither source dispersion nor covariance.
The age factor is independently calibrated and is not fitted to the Kovacs or Wolsk validation series; incomplete validation agreement must remain visible.
Ages outside 18-85 years are rejected rather than extrapolated.
PAWP is used as a surrogate for left-atrial pressure; the nominal resting sink remains fixed unless an observed boundary is supplied.
Transit time and right/left perfusion split remain fixed during exercise.
Gas exchange, biochemical exchange, lobar recruitment, autoregulation, disease, sex, within-band age variation, and patient-specific anatomy are outside this version.
